name: Pierre Poilievre
role: Leader of the Conservative Party of Canada and Leader of the Opposition (since 2022); MP since 2004
summary: Poilievre is a Canadian conservative and free-market populist who campaigns on cutting taxes and spending, axing the carbon tax, building pipelines, tougher sentencing and caps on immigration. He votes against most Liberal firearms, drug and Indigenous-rights bills, supports Canada's NATO and US ties, and as a younger MP voted against same-sex marriage.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Attacks Liberal deficits and pledges a dollar-for-dollar rule and spending caps.

close-ties-china.rationale: Says China is not a substitute for the US and that Canada should deal with China only where prudent, citing its interference and hostage-taking.

collective-defense.rationale: Recalls approvingly Canada's response to the invocation of NATO's Article 5 after 9/11 and pledges to honour NATO commitments.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Says Canada must strengthen alliances with NATO partners and meet its NATO commitments.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Voted against Bill C-69, the Impact Assessment Act, which fossil-fuel project developers opposed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Wants nuclear plants legalised and approved and civilian nuclear technology and uranium exported, but does not speak of funding construction.

farm-price-support.rationale: Names supply-managed farmers among those he would protect in trade talks.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Voted for Bill C-34 strengthening Investment Canada Act review of foreign investments in sensitive sectors.

free-trade.rationale: Calls free trade between Canada and the US an unqualified success and urges tearing down tariff walls and promoting 'free trade among free nations'.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: Endorses Adam Smith's line that commerce should be a bond of union and friendship between nations and says it holds today.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Voted against the Cannabis Act (C-45), which legalised cannabis.

limit-guns.rationale: Voted against Bills C-21 and C-71, the Liberals' firearms-control bills, and for ending the long-gun registry.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Voted for the Safe Streets and Communities Act, which added mandatory minimums, and against C-5, which repealed them.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Praises the free enterprise system, 'free markets, free trade, free nations' and a competition-based economy over carve-outs and bailouts.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Asks whether business should earn by the best product or the best lobbyist and pledges to cut corporate welfare and carve-outs.

open-borders.rationale: Calls the Liberals' policy a 'failed experiment with open borders' and says immigration must be controlled.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Pledges criminal-code penalties for tearing down or defacing statues and monuments.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Pledges to restore and protect national monuments and to celebrate rather than cancel Canada's history.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Wants a real cap on immigration and 'very hard caps' with more people leaving than arriving for a time, while still inviting 'the right people in the right numbers'.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Repeatedly pledges to cut back foreign aid to reduce spending.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted against the Civil Marriage Act at third reading in 2005 and for the 2006 motion to restore the traditional definition of marriage; as an MP he voted for no change since. (He has said since 2024 that he would uphold same-sex marriage, but that is words, and the votes are his record.)

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Voted against the firearms bills C-21 and C-71 and for ending the long-gun registry, which fits keeping lawful private ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted for Bill C-51, which expanded information-sharing and other powers for counter-terrorism.

voter-id.rationale: Voted for the Fair Elections Act (C-23), which tightened identification requirements for voting.

notes: Themes searched: votes in every parliament since 2004 (ourcommons.ca divisions on marriage, firearms, sentencing, drugs, security, elections, Indigenous rights, labour, health, energy), party-published speech transcripts 2025-26, and press reports of pledges on abortion, immigration, notwithstanding clause, UNRWA and the Bank of Canada. Many statements are null because he has not addressed them. Same-sex marriage: his 2005-06 votes are his record; he has said since 2024 he would uphold it. Abortion: he pledges not to legislate (words, no record fetched), so left null.
